'''Fam''' ([fám]<ref name="Idiatov">Idiatov, Dmitry, Mark Van de Velde, Tope Olagunju and Bitrus Andrew. 2017. ''[http://idiatov.mardi.myds.me/talks/2017_CALL_AdaGram_Survey_Results.pdf Results of the first AdaGram survey in Adamawa and Taraba States, Nigeria]''. 47th Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics (CALL) (Leiden, Netherlands).</ref>) is an endangered<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fam Language (FAM) |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/fam/ |website=Ethnologue}}</ref> [[Bantoid language]], spoken by less than 500 in [[Bali, Nigeria|Bali LGA]], [[Taraba State]], [[Nigeria]].

== Name ==
The speakers call themselves Fam, and their language either Fam or Awol Fam, although outsiders call the language Koŋa, Kɔŋa or Konga.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Blench |first=Roger |url=https://rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/Nigeria/Atlas%20of%20Nigerian%20Languages%202020.pdf |title=An Atlas of Nigerian Languages |year=2020 |pages=30, 112}}</ref>

== Demographics ==

=== Speakers ===
In 2016, the language had less than 500 speakers.<ref name=":1" />

Fam is recorded as having either 1000, or less than 1000 speakers in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-07-03 |title=Fam {{!}} Ethnologue |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/fam/ |access-date=2025-03-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703210321/https://www.ethnologue.com/language/fam/ |archive-date=3 July 2019 }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> However, according to linguist [[Roger Blench]], it did not have more than 500 speakers when it was recorded in 1984.<ref name=":0" />

=== Area spoken ===
The language was previously thought to be spoken in the single village of Sabon Gida.<ref name=":0" /> However, according to later research, it is actually spoken in multiple villages.<ref name="Idiatov" />

== Classification ==
Fam is unclassified within the [[Bantoid languages|Bantoid family]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Fam |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/famm1241 |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref>

[[Roger Blench|Blench]] (1993) classifies Fam as a [[Mambiloid languages|Mambiloid language]], within the [[Northern Bantoid languages|Northern Bantoid]] family. It is classed there as likely related particularly to [[Ndoro language|Ndoro]], on the basis of a few [[Cognate|cognates]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Blench |first=Roger M. |date=1993 |title=An outline classification of the Mambiloid languages |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/114869 |journal=Journal of West African Languages |volume=23 |issue=1 |pages=109}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Likewise, Dimmendaal and Voeltz (2007) classify it as a member of the Mambiloid group.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Dimmendaal |first1=Gerrit Jan |title=Endangered languages of Africa and the Middle East |last2=Voeltz |first2=Erhard |pages=613}}</ref> However, Blench (2014) revises his former opinion, stating there is not enough data for a classification and that the claim of a relation to Ndoro is very weak. He concludes Fam is best treated as an isolated Bantoid language.<ref name=":0" /> Still, Blench (2020) lists it as a Mambiloid language, most closely related to Ndoro.<ref name=":1" />

== Grammar ==
A minimal [[Grammar book|grammar]] of the language was written by Tope Olagunjo Demilade in 2017.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Olagunjo Demilade |first=Tope |title=The Fam Language of Taraba State: Basic Description and Grammatical Analysis |date=2017 |degree=masters |publisher=Malete, Ilorin: Kwara State University |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/575636}}</ref>

== Wordlist ==
This wordlist comes from Blench (2014), although note that the words lack [[Tone (linguistics)|tone]] markers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Blench, Roger 2014 |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/672366 |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=glottolog.org |language=en}}</ref>

Many of the words have no clear [[etymology]]. There are [[Cognate|cognates]] with [[Mambiloid languages]], but this cannot be considered proof of a genetic connection as they are often with words that are isolated in Mambiloid languages. For example, "leopard" is {{lang|fam|asar}} in Fam and {{lang|mcj|sɛre}} in [[Mvanip language|Mvanip]]; this may be evidence of a shared [[Substrate (linguistics)|substrate]]. Many words have a [[plural]] [[suffix]] -bə, resembling many Mambiloid languages but also many [[Dakoid languages]].<ref name=":0" />

In the phonology, there is evidence of contact with [[Jukun Takum language|Jukun]], but no good evidence for classification as a [[Jukunoid languages|Jukunoid language]]. Note the [[prefix]] a- found in some plurals, like the Jukunoid languages; many singular nouns also seem to have this prefix. The [[Phone (phonetics)|phone]] /θ/ is present, characteristic of Jukunoid languages (but unusual for Mambiloid languages).<ref name=":0" />

There are common words shared with [[Upper Cross River languages]] (e.g. "one" is {{lang|fam|wuni}} in Fam, {{lang|agb|wɔ̀ní}} in [[Gbo language|Gbo]] and {{lang|mfn|wɔ̀nɔ́}} in [[Mbembe language|Mbembe]]), but again these are not considered proof of relation here.<ref name=":0" />

The words for 'man' and 'women' both have [[Suppletion|suppletive]]-seeming plurals, a common West African [[areal feature]].<ref name=":0" />
